newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Embattled Taleban impose harsher curfew on Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Embattled Taleban impose harsher curfew on Kabul.

text.p: The Islamic Taleban militia, harried by former government forces north of Kabul, tightened a curfew on the Afghan capital on Friday, Kabul radio said.
The Taleban-controlled radio, monitored in Islamabad, said a night curfew must be strictly observed from nine p.m. to five a.m. It gave no reason for the announcement.
Kabul has been under night curfew for the past 17 years of strife in Afghanistan, but enforcement has been patchy.
After the Taleban seized Kabul on September 27 they made no announcement about a curfew, though cautious residents and foreigners behaved as though it remained in force.
Taleban militiamen assaulted and detained a Swiss member of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) as he was walking home at 11 p.m. on Monday. The ICRC protested.
The radio, now calling itself Radio Afghanistan, Voice of Sharia (Islamic law), also said anyone venturing near designated sensitive areas of the city would be seriously punished.
Mullah Malang, an Islamabad-based Taleban spokesman, said the new rules were meant for everyone, but particularly "journalists who make wrong reports". He did not elaborate.

Government forces loyal to ousted government military leader Ahmad Shah Masood took the fight to Taleban troops on Friday, battling along a vital stretch of highway between Kabul and the Salang Pass that links it to the north, witnesses said.
